forces.title: Increasing integration of AI into application software products
forces.description: AI is becoming deeply embedded into technology products, platforms, and decision-making, offering application software providers (IN080201) opportunities to redefine value. With 100% of tech companies starting AI initiatives and 90% in active deployment, AI accounts for 21-40% of digital value. This drives demand for AI-enabled ERP, CRM, HCM, and vertical SaaS, accelerating innovation and competitive advantage. India's AI market is projected to grow to USD 131.31 billion by 2032 at a 42.2% CAGR, further boosting AI-powered application software.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: India emerging as global tech product and IP development hub
forces.description: India is increasingly becoming a global hub for tech product and IP development, moving beyond enterprise servicing to enterprise software solutions. This is supported by cyber GCCs shifting from support roles to creating new innovation and IP, and a vibrant startup ecosystem with 89% of new startups incorporating AI into their products. This structural shift provides a strong foundation and growth opportunity for Application Software companies (IN080201) based in India to develop, own, and export their software IP globally.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Robust talent pool for software development and AI
forces.description: India boasts the world's largest developer workforce with over 5.4 million software engineers and produces 500,000 new graduates annually, ensuring a consistent influx of talent for the application software sector. India also leads globally in AI talent acquisition (33% annual hiring rate) and skill penetration. This deep and growing talent pool, especially in AI and next-generation technologies, provides a significant competitive advantage and enables sustained growth and innovation for Application Software companies in India.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Government funding and policy support for AI ecosystem
forces.description: The Indian government is actively fostering the AI ecosystem with significant initiatives. The IndiaAI Mission has an outlay of Rs 10,372 crore (US$ 1.25 billion) and the Union Budget 2025-26 sanctioned Rs 2,000 crore (US$ 232 million) for AI adoption and infrastructure. Additional schemes boost private-sector R&D and innovation. These investments, alongside the establishment of AI Centres of Excellence and support for startups, create a conducive environment for the development and adoption of AI-powered application software.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Strong demand for legacy system modernization with AI
forces.description: Enterprises are actively prioritizing legacy system modernization and AI-driven transformation. Over 70% of global CXOs consider mainframe or legacy modernization a strategic business priority. This creates substantial demand for new, AI-enabled application software (ERP, CRM, vertical SaaS) that can replace outdated systems, integrate real-time data, and prepare businesses for future AI capabilities. Partnerships like Deloitte-Confluent aim to help enterprises transition, boosting opportunities for application software vendors in this space.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Shift towards platform-based strategies and product-led growth
forces.description: Organizations are increasingly adopting platform-based strategies focused on standardization, reuse, and interoperability. This fosters non-linear growth through products and automation. This trend directly benefits application software providers (IN080201) offering integrated, scalable, platform-based solutions (e.g., SaaS platforms) that can streamline enterprise operations and enable rapid iteration. The focus on 'XaaS technologies' (Everything as a Service) with high future adoption further underlines this shift, favoring subscription-based application software models.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: GCCs driving strategic value and AI-native application development
forces.description: India-based Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are evolving beyond cost-efficiency to become strategic value drivers, owning core retail and CPG processes like merchandising, supply chain, and customer experience. They are embedding analytics, AI, and agentic capabilities to improve decision quality and scalability. This shift means GCCs are actively developing and integrating sophisticated application software for their parent organizations. The next phase of GCC evolution to 'AI-realized' and outcome-driven operations represents a significant demand source for advanced, AI-native application software.
forces.source_title: How India GCCs are driving core retail and CPG value

forces.title: BFSI demand for AI-powered and digitally enhanced application software
forces.description: BFSI is a key vertical driving IT expenditure, with investment in new technologies required for competitive advantage beyond cost reduction. The RBI suggests Generative AI can enhance banking operations by up to 46%, and Indian BFSI firms are consolidating IT platforms with a focus on AI-era capabilities. This translates to increased demand for AI-powered application software (ERP, CRM, specialized vertical SaaS for finance) that can deliver advanced functionalities for risk management, operational efficiency, and digital payment security within the financial sector.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Challenges in scaling AI and technology programs across enterprises
forces.description: Despite widespread AI adoption (100% of tech firms starting initiatives), only about 10% report achieving AI at scale with consistent ROI. The primary constraint is not funding or intent, but execution, with challenges including integration complexity, operating model limitations, and organizational structure. For Application Software providers, this means that while demand for AI-enabled software is high, ensuring successful, enterprise-wide deployment and demonstrating tangible ROI at scale remains a significant hurdle and a key risk to adoption and revenue recognition.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Heightened cybersecurity and third-party risk for application software vendors
forces.description: RBI’s new Master Directions consolidate technology governance and cybersecurity requirements across regulated entities, significantly increasing compliance burdens. Third-party technology arrangements are a major focus, meaning Application Software vendors selling to BFSI clients will face heightened scrutiny and risk management requirements. Furthermore, global boards track software supply chain security risk as a top concern. This necessitates greater investment in security-by-design, robust audit trails, and compliance capabilities for IN080201 companies to mitigate risks and maintain market access, particularly in regulated sectors.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: Significant AI security gaps in BFSI hindering application software deployment
forces.description: Indian BFSI firms show significant immaturity in AI security, with 24% not formally assessing any major AI security risks and less than one-third deploying core AI security controls at scale. There are wide gaps in AI governance, agent monitoring, and guardrails for agent actions compared to global peers. This poses a substantial risk for Application Software (IN080201) vendors integrating AI into their products for BFSI clients, as they must navigate an environment with low security maturity, potentially increasing their own risk exposure or requiring them to build more comprehensive security features by default.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity in the Age of AI

forces.title: Integration complexity and legacy systems impede technology ROI
forces.description: A significant proportion of technology organizations (60%) report that legacy systems and processes reduce the effectiveness of technology investment. Integration complexity, operating model limitations, and organizational structure are key factors creating barriers to scaling. For Application Software providers (IN080201), this means that even advanced solutions can struggle to deliver full ROI due to the challenge of integrating with existing, often outdated, enterprise IT landscapes. This increases implementation costs and timeframes, acting as a headwind to rapid adoption and value realization.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Shift to outcome-based and subscription revenue models
forces.description: The IT industry is undergoing a structural shift from 'per-FTE' contracts to outcome-based models, driven by AI-driven productivity gains (20-40%). Clients are increasingly demanding pay-for-results, prompting companies to adapt by offering fixed-price, subscription, and usage-based deals. This transition directly aligns with the revenue models (ARR, subscription/license) characteristic of Application Software (IN080201) companies, cementing this as the preferred approach and driving incumbents to restructure their offerings towards product-led, value-driven engagements.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Agentic AI redefining enterprise interaction and operationalization
forces.description: Agentic AI, with autonomous agents initiating actions and interacting with enterprise applications, is fundamentally reshaping how enterprises create value. This necessitates a rethinking of technology architectures, governance models, and operating principles. For Application Software (IN080201), this means a structural shift towards applications designed for agent interaction, requiring robust AI governance, enterprise-grade data foundations, and human oversight. Competitive advantage will increasingly depend on the ability to operationalize intelligence safely and at scale through agent-empowered applications.
forces.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

viewpoints.title: AI adoption key to unlocking new business models and competitive advantage
viewpoints.description: KPMG notes that technology companies are focusing on leveraging AI investments for sustained value. AI's deep embedding into products, platforms, and decision-making offers a significant opportunity for leaders to redefine value creation. This involves not only improving efficiency but also enabling new business models, accelerating innovation, and strengthening competitive advantage through AI-powered application software. However, scaling AI consistently across enterprises remains a complex challenge, indicating a gap between widespread adoption and fully realized ROI.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

viewpoints.title: Effective Agentic AI deployment crucial for next competitive advantage
viewpoints.description: KPMG asserts that the next wave of disruption from Agentic AI will stem from its effective deployment within complex enterprise environments, rather than just building powerful models. Competitive differentiation for application software providers will depend on how quickly they can operationalize AI and embed it into business processes safely and at scale. Indian enterprises are urged to move beyond experimentation, focusing on strong deployment capabilities, trusted AI governance, and enterprise-grade data foundations to achieve measurable business impact and competitive advantage.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

viewpoints.title: India's IT sector transitioning from services to enterprise software solutions
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights that India’s IT sector is at an inflection point, evolving from primarily providing enterprise services to developing and offering enterprise software solutions. This structural shift signifies a maturity in the Indian tech ecosystem, emphasizing product ownership and IP creation. It signals a growing capability and focus within India on developing proprietary application software, which aligns directly with the core definition of IN080201 and positions India as a significant player in the global application software market.
viewpoints.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

viewpoints.title: India's GCCs are evolving to strategic, AI-native value drivers
viewpoints.description: EY states that India-based Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in sectors like Retail and Consumer Products are transforming from cost-efficiency centers into strategic value drivers. They are increasingly owning core processes such as merchandising, supply chain, and customer experience, and embedding analytics, AI, and agentic capabilities into their operations. The next phase of GCC evolution is expected to be AI-native, outcome-driven, and deeply integrated with enterprise strategy and partner ecosystems, creating a strong impetus for advanced application software development and integration.
viewpoints.source_title: How India GCCs are driving core retail and CPG value

demand_drivers.description: Propelled by sectors such as BFSI, manufacturing, government, software, and media, indicating broad demand for cloud-delivered solutions including application software.

market_sizing.methodology: India's public cloud services market reached US$ 10.9 billion in 2024, expected to reach US$ 30.4 billion by 2029 at a CAGR of 22.6%, propelled chiefly by sectors such as BFSI, manufacturing, government, software, and media. While this is cloud infrastructure (IN080202), its growth underpins the scalability and delivery of SaaS application software.
market_sizing.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Rapid growth and adoption of AI technologies across various sectors in India, including enterprise and consumer applications.
Government initiatives like the IndiaAI Mission and significant investments fostering AI research, infrastructure, and skill development.
Approximately 89% of startups launched in the last year incorporating AI into their products or services, driving embedded AI solutions.

market_sizing.methodology: The Indian AI market is expected to grow to USD 131.31 billion by 2032 at a CAGR of 42.2%. This market size reflects the broader adoption of AI across industries, significantly driving demand for AI-enabled application software that integrates AI capabilities into enterprise and consumer solutions.
market_sizing.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Indian companies are actively investing internationally to expand their global footprint and enhance their global delivery centers for software products.
India boasts the world's largest developer workforce (5.4 million software engineers) and a consistent influx of new graduates, ensuring a robust talent pool for product development.
India's IT sector is moving from enterprise servicing to developing and offering proprietary enterprise software solutions and products.

market_sizing.methodology: The Indian software product industry is expected to reach US$ 101.64 billion by 2030. This directly relates to Application Software (IN080201) as it encompasses companies that own software IP and generate revenue from subscriptions/licenses.
market_sizing.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Global demand for Indian software products
demand_drivers.description: The consistent export share highlights sustained international demand for software products developed in India, aligning with the IN080201 definition of companies owning software IP for global use.

market_sizing.methodology: In FY25, software products and engineering and R&D (ER&D) exports accounted for 8% of total IT exports, which indicates the current contribution of application software and related product development activities to India's overall IT export landscape.
